List it in `removed` with a reason - CI rejects a title that disappears otherwise.

titles.title: Resurrection Blvd.
titles.note: Created and run by Dennis E. Leoni (Imagen Foundation's Norman Lear Writer's Award, honoring a Latino writer); a Mexican American boxing family in East LA, Showtime 2000-2002. breakthrough: the first weekly one-hour drama series to predominantly feature Latinos both in front of and behind the camera. Source: UCLA CSRC collection

titles.title: Cuestión de fe

titles.title: Cocote

titles.title: Bantú Mama

titles.title: Carajita
titles.note: Silvina Schnicer (Argentine) and Ulises Porra (Barcelona-born; Spain is in scope) wrote and directed; a nanny and the daughter of a wealthy Dominican family. Source: Screen Daily. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: El Suspiro del Silencio
titles.note: Directed by Alfonso Quijada - heritage not confirmed by a source, so no led_by yet. about_community: a campesina coffee picker in rural El Salvador. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: El silencio de Neto
titles.note: Luis Argueta (Guatemalan) directed and co-wrote; a boy's coming of age during the 1954 coup. breakthrough: Guatemala's first Oscar submission. Source: Wikipedia. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Las marimbas del infierno
titles.note: Julio Hernández Cordón wrote and directed; a marimba player and a heavy-metal musician in post-war Guatemala City. Source: Wikipedia, Variety. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Gasolina
titles.note: Julio Hernández Cordón (raised in Guatemala; 'Guatemala's Julio Hernández Cordón' - Variety) wrote and directed; post-war Guatemala City youth. Source: Wikipedia, Variety. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Cadejo Blanco
titles.note: Directed by Justin Lerner (Boston-born, not Latino - no led_by). about_community: a Guatemala City girl infiltrates a gang in Puerto Barrios, cast largely with former gang members. Source: Variety. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: No hay tierra sin dueño
titles.note: Sami Kafati (born Tegucigalpa) wrote and directed; a rancher's rule over the land. Made 1984, released 2003. breakthrough: the first Honduran feature film. Source: IMDb bio, La Nación, AramcoWorld. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Amor y frijoles
titles.note: Co-directed by Mathew Kodath (from India) and Hernán Pereira (heritage not confirmed) - no led_by. about_community: food vendors in Ojojona, Honduras. Source: Casa de América, La Prensa. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: El Xendra
titles.note: Juan Carlos Fanconi (born Tegucigalpa) directed; Maya-inflected science fiction - the premise doesn't depend on a community, so no about_community. Source: es.wikipedia. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Morazán
titles.note: Hispano Durón (Honduran) wrote and directed; the last week of Francisco Morazán. breakthrough: Honduras' first-ever Oscar entry. Source: Wikipedia, Remezcla. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: La Yuma

titles.title: Palabras mágicas

titles.title: Box 25
titles.note: Directed by Mercedes Arias and Delfina Vidal - heritage not confirmed by a source, so no led_by yet. about_community: letters from the West Indian workers who built the Panama Canal. Source: Wikipedia, Variety. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: Salsipuedes
titles.note: Directed by Ricardo Aguilar Navarro and Manuel Rodríguez - heritage not confirmed by a source, so no led_by yet. about_community: three generations in Panama City's El Chorrillo. Panama's Oscar entry. Source: Wikipedia, Variety. Latin American cinema list, Phase 2.

titles.title: The Gold Seekers

titles.title: NN

titles.title: Los peloteros

titles.title: Cayo

titles.title: October

titles.title: The Return

titles.title: Viaje

titles.title: The Family

titles.title: Mar.IA

Argentine horror; premiered at Sitges 2023-10-12, released in Argentina 2024-06-13. No about_community (rule #4): a genre story about a film shoot, not Latino community experience. No breakthrough: festival awards but no citable first. Set around an erotic-film shoot, not adult content itself (ADULT_CONTENT_POLICY).

titles.title: Prefiero la muerte
titles.note: Created, written and directed by Sebastián Sariñana, a Mexican TV director (FirstShowing; PRODU); TMDB credits him as director on all 8 episodes. Mexican Prime Video original (Amazon MGM Studios, Tigre Pictures, Pez Caja), premiered 2026-10-02. No about_community (rule #4): a teen zombie comedy whose provincial-town setting isn't the subject. No starring: the creator tags already cover it. Lead is Diego Bernal (Archie), missing from TMDB's cast list.

titles.title: Suárez
titles.note: Documentary (40 min) on Monterrey-born NASCAR driver Daniel Suárez's homecoming at the 2025 Mexico City race, premiered on FS1 2026-09-17 for Hispanic Heritage Month (TMDB lists a 2026-05-29 release). produced_by: executive produced by Wilmer Valderrama through his WV Alternative, a co-producer with NASCAR Studios and FOX Sports (FOX Sports press release via Jayski). about_community: a Mexican-born driver's return to Mexico as a cultural symbol is the subject, not a backdrop. No led_by: director Mario Díaz's background is unverified. Deferred until TMDB populated its release date.

titles.title: Tigers Are Not Afraid
titles.note: Written and directed by Issa López, Mexican (Wikipedia; MoMA). Children orphaned by cartel violence in a Mexican city; the drug war's toll on its children is the subject. Premiered at Fantastic Fest 2017 (Best Horror Director); two Ariel Awards.

titles.title: Sujo
titles.note: Written and directed by Astrid Rondero and Fernanda Valadez, Mexican filmmakers (TMDB credits; Cinema Tropical). A cartel gunman's orphaned son growing up in rural Mexico. Sundance 2024 World Cinema Dramatic Grand Jury Prize; Mexico's Oscar submission (Deadline). US/FR/MX co-production.

titles.title: Tótem
titles.note: Written and directed by Lila Avilés, Mexican (TMDB credits; Screen Daily). A girl's day at her dying father's birthday party. Berlinale competition, Ecumenical Jury Prize; Mexico's Oscar submission, shortlisted. No about_community (rule #4): a family drama whose Mexico City setting isn't the subject.

titles.title: Los lobos
titles.note: Directed and co-written by Samuel Kishi, born in Guadalajara (Pragda; Wikipedia). Semi-autobiographical: two Mexican boys left alone while their immigrant mother works in Albuquerque. Berlinale 2020 Generation Kplus Grand Prix. TMDB dates it 2020-06-19; Wikipedia gives 2019.

titles.title: Cronos
titles.note: Guillermo del Toro's debut feature; he wrote and directed it (TMDB credits). Mexican horror. No about_community (rule #4): genre story.

titles.title: Pedro Páramo
titles.note: Directed by Rodrigo Prieto in his native Mexico, his feature directing debut (Wikipedia; Filmmaker Magazine). No created_by: screenplay by Mateo Gil (Spanish) from Juan Rulfo's novel, and a source novelist doesn't count (rule #1). Premiered at TIFF 2024; Netflix.

titles.title: La niña santa
titles.note: Written and directed by Lucrecia Martel, Argentine (TMDB credits); her La Ciénaga is already in the canon. No about_community (rule #4): a coming-of-age drama set in Salta, not about community experience.

titles.title: Ponyboi
titles.note: Directed by Esteban Arango, Colombian American, born in Bogotá (Wikipedia); written by and starring River Gallo, Salvadoran-American (Rutgers Latino Studies; Berlinale Talents). Premiered at Sundance 2024; TMDB dates it 2025-06-27. No about_community: an intersex sex worker's story whose Latino context isn't the subject.

titles.ref: Rita Moreno: Just a Girl Who Decided to Go for It (2021)
titles.title: Rita Moreno: Just a Girl Who Decided to Go for It
titles.note: Documentary directed by Mariem Pérez Riera, Puerto Rican (Wikipedia; Bay State Banner). Rita Moreno's life from Puerto Rico to Hollywood, centered on the racism and typecasting she faced. Premiered at Sundance 2021; PBS American Masters.

titles.title: Raising Victor Vargas
titles.note: Directed by Peter Sollett, written with Eva Vives - no Latino creative control. Shot in the Dominican community of the Lower East Side with untrained actors from it (Wikipedia); Dominican teen life is the subject. No starring: Victor Rasuk's own heritage isn't confirmed by a source yet. Premiered at Cannes 2002; TMDB dates the 2003 US release.

titles.title: Quinceañera
titles.note: Directed and written by Richard Glatzer and Wash Westmoreland - no Latino creative control. Two Mexican American cousins in gentrifying Echo Park; the community is the subject. Sundance 2006 Dramatic Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award (Wikipedia; Deadline). TMDB lists ES as origin country, which looks wrong.

titles.title: I Carry You With Me
titles.note: Directed by Heidi Ewing (not Latina); co-writer Alan Page Arriaga's background is unverified, so no created_by. True story of an undocumented gay couple from Puebla building a life in New York; migration and Mexican family are the subject. Sundance 2020 NEXT Audience Award (NPR; Variety). TMDB dates it 2021-06-25.

titles.title: Los silencios
titles.note: Written and directed by Beatriz Seigner, Brazilian, born in São Paulo (Wikipedia; Mostra de São Paulo). A mother and her children who fled Colombia's armed conflict settle on an Amazon border island; displacement by the conflict is the subject. Premiered at Cannes Directors' Fortnight 2018; TMDB dates it 2019 (Brazilian release). Colombia/Brazil/France co-production. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Rasga Coração
titles.note: Directed by Jorge Furtado, Brazilian, born in Porto Alegre (pt.wikipedia); he co-wrote it with Vicente Moreno and Ana Luíza Azevedo (TMDB credits). A former activist who resisted Brazil's military regime clashes with his son; the dictatorship's legacy is the subject (same reading as I'm Still Here). Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: O Filme da Minha Vida
titles.note: Directed by Selton Mello, Brazilian, born in Passos, Minas Gerais (pt.wikipedia); screenplay by Mello and Marcelo Vindicato (TMDB credits), from Antonio Skármeta's novel - the source novelist doesn't count (rule #1), and isn't needed. No about_community (rule #4): a coming-of-age family drama whose 1960s rural-Brazil setting isn't the subject. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Últimos días en La Habana
titles.note: Directed by Fernando Pérez, Cuban (Wikipedia); co-written with Abel Rodríguez (TMDB credits). A man waiting for a US visa and his bedridden HIV-positive friend in a changing Havana; Cuban life and emigration are the subject. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: O Menino e o Mundo
titles.note: Written and directed by Alê Abreu, Brazilian, born in São Paulo (pt.wikipedia). Animated; premiered at Ottawa 2013-09-20, released in Brazil 2014-01-17 (TMDB dates it 2014). Nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 88th Academy Awards; Annecy Cristal for best feature (Wikipedia). No breakthrough: no sourced 'first' (the precedent is a documented first, e.g. El silencio de Neto). No about_community (rule #6): an allegory of rural Brazil meeting the globalized city - arguable, so left out. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Libertador
titles.note: Directed by Alberto Arvelo, Venezuelan, born in Caracas (IMDb; EcuRed). Simón Bolívar's campaigns for South American independence; a Latin American historical figure as subject, same reading as Morazán and Neruda. No created_by: screenplay by Timothy J. Sexton (TMDB credits). No starring: Edgar Ramírez (Venezuelan) leads, but led_by already covers it. Premiered at TIFF 2013; Venezuela's Oscar submission, January shortlist for the 87th Academy Awards (Wikipedia). Venezuela/Spain. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Che: Part One
titles.note: Directed by Steven Soderbergh; screenplay by Peter Buchman and Benjamin A. van der Veen (Wikipedia) - no Latino director or writer, so no led_by/created_by. produced_by: Benicio del Toro (Puerto Rican) produced with Laura Bickford, optioned the source biography with her and spent years developing the project before Soderbergh was attached (Wikipedia). about_community: Che Guevara and the Cuban Revolution are the subject, same reading as Morazán. Del Toro also leads (Cannes 2008 Best Actor); no separate starring tag (rule: for when the performer is the only connection). Primarily in Spanish. Suggested by the editor; not from a tracking list.

titles.title: Che: Part Two
titles.note: Second half of Soderbergh's Che (2008): Guevara's Bolivian campaign. Same credits and reasoning as Che: Part One - no Latino director or writer (Soderbergh; Buchman and van der Veen); produced_by Benicio del Toro (Puerto Rican) with Laura Bickford; about_community, Latin American revolutionary history as subject. Suggested by the editor; not from a tracking list.

titles.title: O Lobo Atrás da Porta
titles.note: Written and directed by Fernando Coimbra, Brazilian, born in Ribeirão Preto (pt.wikipedia). His debut feature: a kidnapping thriller. Horizontes Latinos prize at San Sebastián; best director at Guadalajara (pt.wikipedia). No about_community (rule #4): a crime story whose Rio setting isn't the subject. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Tatuagem
titles.note: Written and directed by Hilton Lacerda, Brazilian, born in Recife (pt.wikipedia). A queer cabaret troupe in late-1970s Recife and a soldier drawn to it, under the military dictatorship's repression; that repression is the subject, not a backdrop (same reading as I'm Still Here). Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: La demora
titles.note: Directed by Rodrigo Plá, Uruguayan, born in Montevideo (Wikipedia); written by Laura Santullo, Uruguayan, born in Montevideo (es.wikipedia). A caregiver abandons her father, whose memory is failing. Premiered at the Berlinale 2012; Uruguay's Oscar submission, not shortlisted (Wikipedia). No about_community (rule #4): a family drama whose Montevideo setting isn't the subject. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: O Céu de Suely
titles.note: Directed by Karim Aïnouz, Brazilian, born in Fortaleza (Wikipedia); he co-wrote it with Felipe Bragança, Simone Lima and Mauricio Zacharias (TMDB credits). An abandoned young mother in Ceará raffles a night with herself to leave town. No about_community (rule #6): the Northeast setting matters, but whether the community is the subject is arguable, so left out. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Gigante
titles.note: Written and directed by Adrián Biniez, an Argentine director living in Uruguay (Wikipedia). A supermarket security guard's obsession with a night-shift cleaner. Berlinale 2009: Silver Bear Jury Grand Prix, Alfred Bauer Prize and best first feature (Wikipedia). No breakthrough: awards, but no sourced 'first'. No about_community (rule #4): a romance whose Montevideo setting isn't the subject. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: El Amparo
titles.note: Directed by Rober Calzadilla, Venezuelan, born in Maturín (Cinema Tropical); written by Karin Valecillos, Venezuelan (The Objective), from their play 29/10/88. The 1988 El Amparo massacre, in which the Venezuelan army killed fishermen it accused of being Colombian guerrillas; the survivors' ordeal is the subject. Venezuela/Colombia; Venezuela's Goya candidate for Ibero-American film, 2018 (Wikipedia). TMDB dates the US release 2017. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: La delgada línea amarilla
titles.note: Written and directed by Celso R. García, born in Mexico City (Sensacine); his debut feature, premiered at Guadalajara 2015 (14 Ariel nominations). The tracking CSV listed it as Peruvian; it's Mexican. Guillermo del Toro produced it, but no produced_by: the extent of his role isn't sourced (rule #6), and led_by/created_by already qualify it. No about_community (rule #6): road workers in rural Mexico, arguable as subject vs setting. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: La jaula de oro
titles.note: Directed by Diego Quemada-Díez, a Spanish-born Mexican filmmaker, born in Burgos (Wikipedia) - Spanish heritage qualifies (CRITERIA, Scope of 'Latino'); he co-wrote it with Lucía Carreras and Gibrán Portela (TMDB credits; AFI Fest). Guatemalan teenagers migrating north through Mexico; Central American migration is the subject. Cannes Un Certain Regard 2013, A Certain Talent prize (Wikipedia). Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: Entre nos
titles.note: Written and directed by Paola Mendoza, a Colombian immigrant (Kripalu bio), with Gloria La Morte as an equal co-director and co-writer (TMDB credits; Tribeca) - not a co-director under a non-Latino lead, so led_by holds (rule #3). Semi-autobiographical: a Colombian mother abandoned in New York raising two children, based on Mendoza's own mother's arrival (Tribeca). Mendoza also leads; no starring, since about_community already covers it. Tribeca 2009 premiere. Tracking CSV (100, 158 lists).

titles.title: La bestia
titles.note: Documentary written and directed by Pedro Ultreras, Mexican, born in Durango (Dialnet academic article; IMDb), a former Univision reporter; some listings add Hiram Gonzalez as co-director. Central American migrants riding the freight train through Mexico; migration is the subject. Tracking CSV (El Salvador lists).

titles.title: Lienzo en blanco
titles.note: Co-directed by Leslie Gabriela Ortiz, a Salvadoran filmmaker based in Toronto, who co-wrote it with Libia Perez (TMDB credits), and Gabriela Cruz. Salvadoran feature, premiered at the Chicago Latino Film Festival 2022; an art-therapy workshop for survivors of violence becomes a bond to bring a rapist to justice. No about_community (rule #6): whether Salvadoran experience is the subject or the setting is arguable. Tracking CSV (El Salvador lists).

titles.title: Hoy
titles.note: Directed by Ricardo B'atz' (Ricardo Landaverde Flores), born in El Salvador in 1986 (Locarno Open Doors); co-written with Leonel Novoa (TMDB credits). Drivers in San Salvador living with the damage of the 12-year civil war; its aftermath is the subject. No 'Today' alias: the exact-title pin would put this film first for any search for the word 'today'. Tracking CSV (El Salvador lists).

titles.title: El hoyo 2
titles.note: Directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia, a Spanish (Basque) director (Wikipedia; Spain is in scope), who co-wrote it with Pedro Rivero, David Desola and Egoitz Moreno (TMDB credits). Sequel to El hoyo (2019): a newcomer to the vertical prison confronts a leader's food-distribution regime. No about_community (rule #4): dystopian allegory, not Latino experience. Requested directly; sci-fi and dystopia list.

titles.title: El hoyo
titles.note: Directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia, a Spanish (Basque) director (Wikipedia; Spain is in scope); screenplay by David Desola, a Spanish screenwriter born in Barcelona (es.wikipedia), with Pedro Rivero. A vertical prison where food descends level by level; class allegory. No about_community (rule #4). TMDB has an unrelated 2005 'El hoyo' - pinned. Sci-fi and dystopia list.

titles.title: Los últimos días
titles.note: Written and directed by Àlex and David Pastor, 'the Spanish brothers' (Moria review of Bird Box Barcelona; TMDB credits; Spain is in scope). An epidemic of agoraphobia traps Barcelona indoors. No about_community (rule #4). TMDB has several other 'Los últimos días' - pinned. Sci-fi and dystopia list.

titles.title: Bird Box Barcelona
titles.note: Written and directed by Àlex and David Pastor, 'the Spanish brothers' (Moria review; Columbia School of the Arts on David Pastor; TMDB credits). Spanish-language Netflix spin-off of Bird Box; Josh Malerman is credited only for the source novel (rule #1), the screenplay is the Pastors'. No about_community (rule #4). Requested directly.

titles.title: El bar
titles.note: Directed by Álex de la Iglesia, 'a Spanish film director, screenwriter, producer' born in Bilbao (Wikipedia), who co-wrote it with Jorge Guerricaechevarría (TMDB credits). Strangers trapped in a Madrid bar after a shooting outside. No about_community (rule #4). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: Fase 7
titles.note: Written and directed by Nicolás Goldbart, 'director, guionista y montajista de cine argentino' (es.wikipedia). A Buenos Aires apartment building under pandemic quarantine; dark comedy. No about_community (rule #4). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: El páramo
titles.note: Directed by Jaime Osorio Márquez, born in Cali, Colombia in 1975 (es.wikipedia), his debut; co-written with Tania Cárdenas Paulsen and Diego Vivanco (TMDB credits). An army squad at a remote mountain outpost. No about_community (rule #4). Pin to 83705: TMDB 800410 is a 2021 Spanish film with the same original title. Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: Los parecidos
titles.note: Written and directed by Isaac Ezban, 'a Mexican film director, writer and producer' born in Mexico City (Wikipedia). Retro sci-fi: travelers stranded at a bus station in 1968 begin to change. No about_community (rule #4). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: Cuando acecha la maldad
titles.note: Written and directed by Demián Rugna, an 'Argentine film director' born in Haedo, Buenos Aires (Wikipedia; TMDB credits him as director and writer). A demonic rot spreads through a rural town. No about_community (rule #4). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: Aterrados
titles.note: Written and directed by Demián Rugna, an 'Argentine film director' (Wikipedia; TMDB credits). Supernatural events in one Buenos Aires neighborhood. Year 2018 per TMDB (the source list said 2017). Second Rugna title in this batch with Cuando acecha la maldad - two is within rule #7. No about_community (rule #4). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: La región salvaje
titles.note: Directed by Amat Escalante, a 'Spanish and Mexican filmmaker', both citizenships (Wikipedia), who co-wrote it with Gibrán Portela (TMDB credits). A family in Guanajuato and a creature in the woods; machismo and homophobia. No about_community pending an editorial call (rule #6). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: Somos lo que hay
titles.note: Written and directed by Jorge Michel Grau, Mexican, born in Mexico City (es.wikipedia). A cannibal family in Mexico City after the father's death. Pin to 50272: TMDB 159128 is Jim Mickle's 2013 US remake. No about_community pending an editorial call (rule #6). Zombie and social-collapse list.

titles.title: El espinazo del diablo
titles.note: Directed by Guillermo del Toro, 'a Mexican filmmaker' born in Guadalajara (Wikipedia), who co-wrote it with David Muñoz and Antonio Trashorras (TMDB credits). A ghost story in an orphanage at the end of the Spanish Civil War. Reverses CANON_TRACKING_MASTER.csv row 73, which excluded it as a 'Spanish director' - del Toro is Mexican, and Spain is in scope anyway. No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list (docs/GENRE_CANDIDATES.csv).

titles.title: Juan de los muertos
titles.note: Written and directed by Alejandro Brugués, an 'Argentine-Cuban director and writer' born in Buenos Aires (Wikipedia; TMDB credits him as director and writer). A zombie outbreak in Havana. about_community is arguable (the satire is of Cuban life, and the Havana setting carries the story - rule #4's test) and left for an editor (rule #6). Genre candidates list.

titles.ref: La casa del fin de los tiempos (2013)
titles.title: La casa del fin de los tiempos
titles.note: Written and directed by Alejandro Hidalgo, a 'cineasta venezolano' (El Diario; Remezcla); his debut. Wikipedia: 'the highest-grossing horror film in Venezuelan history, and the most internationally-distributed Venezuelan film.' A woman returns to the house where her family died thirty years earlier. No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Hombre mirando al sudeste
titles.note: Written and directed by Eliseo Subiela, 'an Argentine film director and writer' born in Buenos Aires (Wikipedia; TMDB credits). A man in a Buenos Aires psychiatric hospital says he is from another planet. Year 1987 per TMDB's Argentine release (the list said 1986). No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Chuzalongo
titles.note: Written and directed by Diego Ortuño, 'el ecuatoriano Diego Ortuño' (cited by Wikipedia; Primicias). Ecuador-Canada-Peru-Spain co-production built on the Andean legend of the Chuzalongo, shot in Cayambe and Otavalo; Ecuador's entry for Best International Feature at the 98th Academy Awards (Wikipedia). Year 2024 per TMDB (the list said 2017). about_community left for an editor (rule #6). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Muere, monstruo, muere
titles.note: Written and directed by Alejandro Fadel, 'director y guionista de cine argentino' born in Tunuyán, Mendoza (es.wikipedia; TMDB credits). Selected for Cannes Un Certain Regard 2018 (es.wikipedia). A rural police officer investigates women found beheaded in the Andes. The list's title 'Muéreme, monstruo' was wrong. No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Veneno para las hadas
titles.note: Directed by Carlos Enrique Taboada, 'a Mexican film director' (Wikipedia, which dates it 1984); TMDB credits him for the screenplay and dates the release 1986. Two girls, one convinced the other is a witch. The source list mislabeled Here Comes the Devil with this title. No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Abre los ojos
titles.note: Directed by Alejandro Amenábar, 'a Chilean-Spanish film director, screenwriter and composer' born in Santiago, Chile (Wikipedia), who co-wrote it with Mateo Gil (TMDB credits). Remade in Hollywood as Vanilla Sky (Wikipedia). No about_community (rule #4). Genre candidates list.

titles.title: Batman Azteca: Choque de imperios
titles.note: Directed by Juan Meza-León, 'a self-taught artist from the port town of Ensenada, Baja CA, Mexico' (El Festival speaker bio), who shares the story credit with Ernie Altbacker; Altbacker wrote the screenplay (Wikipedia). Lead voice Horacio García Rojas as Yohualli Coatl, a 'Mexican actor' (AWN). US-Mexico co-production (Warner Bros. Animation, DC, Ánima, Chatrone), 'completely produced in Mexico' (Wikipedia). An Aztec Batman fighting Cortés's conquest of Tenochtitlán. about_community left for an editor (rule #6): the subject is Mexica history and the conquest, and CRITERIA keeps Indigenous and Latino as distinct categories. Alias 'Batman Azteca', the short title in Mexican press. Requested directly.

titles.title: El Eternauta
titles.note: Created by Bruno Stagnaro, 'un cineasta argentino' born in Buenos Aires (es.wikipedia), who directed every episode and co-wrote it with Ariel Staltari (Wikipedia). Lead Ricardo Darín as Juan Salvo, an 'Argentine actor' born in Buenos Aires (Wikipedia). Netflix series from Argentina, adapted from Héctor Germán Oesterheld and Francisco Solano López's 1957 comic: a toxic snowfall kills millions and survivors in Buenos Aires face an invasion. Season 1 (6 episodes) released 30 April 2025; renewed for a final second season (Wikipedia). about_community left for an editor (rule #6): Buenos Aires carries the story, but it's a science-fiction invasion. Action list, requested directly.

titles.title: Escritor
titles.note: Written and directed by Paula de Luque, an Argentine director born in 1969 who studied at the Universidad del Cine in Buenos Aires (Venice Mostra profile; TMDB credits); she also made Juan y Eva. In 1956 Argentina, the young Rodolfo Walsh witnesses a failed uprising against the military regime and investigates the survivors of the massacre that followed (TMDB). about_community left for an editor (rule #6): Argentine political history carries it, as with El Eternauta. SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Oca
titles.note: Written and directed by Karla Badillo, 'la cineasta mexicana', her first feature (Milenio; TMDB credits). Premiered at TIFF; won the Silver Hugo in Chicago's New Directors competition and best film at Málaga (WOW Film Festival, Milenio). Mexico-Argentina co-production. A young nun is sent to find a new archbishop to save her failing convent, structured on the board game of the goose (Milenio). No about_community (rule #4). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Nuda propiedad
titles.note: Directed by Alberto Utrera, a Madrid-born director and screenwriter (Alcine festival bio), who co-wrote it with Carlos Soria (Cinemanía). Spanish black comedy: a couple in their forties buys a flat under a 'bare ownership' deal and waits for the elderly seller to die (Sensacine). Shot in Madrid and Tenerife. No about_community (rule #4). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Jardim dos Silêncios
titles.note: Written and directed by Henrique Dantas, a 'cineasta baiano' known for documentaries, his first fiction feature (Ingresso.com; TMDB credits). A Black oncologist who left Brazil as a child during the military dictatorship returns to Bahia after his mother's death (Festival do Rio). Brazil-Italy co-production. about_community left for an editor (rule #6). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Casa Pura
titles.note: Directed and written by Bruno Irizarry, 'cineasta puertorriqueño' (200 Cartas, Yerba Buena) (Metro Puerto Rico, Noticel). After Hurricane Maria, Joaquín (Jencarlos Canela) fights to save his family's boutique hotel in Puerto Rico from a buyer and a long-lost will (TMDB); inspired by real events (Noticel). Released in Puerto Rico 12 February 2026. SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Carmela y los caminantes
titles.note: Ecuadorian documentary by Luis Herrera and Esteban Coloma, produced by the cooperative CoopDocs; Special Mention at Sheffield DocFest and opening film of EDOC in Quito (Labocine, Expreso). Carmela, an Afro-Ecuadorian mother of eight near the Colombian border, shelters thousands of Venezuelans crossing on foot (TMDB, Sheffield DocFest). led_by not added: no source confirms the directors' heritage (rule #2). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Comparsa
titles.note: Documentary directed by Vickie Curtis and Doug Anderson, a New York-based filmmaker; Guatemalan director Jayro Bustamante is an executive producer (Labocine, Eye for Film). Sisters Lesli and Lupe Canela Pérez of Ciudad Peronia, Guatemala answer the deaths of 41 girls in a state-run 'Safe Home' fire with a community street comparsa (MSP Film, UNAFF). Won the International First Feature Competition at Sheffield DocFest 2025. No led_by; an executive producer credit isn't produced_by. SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Show Me How to Die
titles.note: Short (14 min). Written and directed by Gerardo Maravilla, a Mexican-American filmmaker born and raised in the San Fernando Valley, made as a Latino Inclusion Fellow (NYLFF 2025; CQNL bio). After her grandmother dies, a grieving Mexican-American woman seeks out a lab that simulates dying (NYLFF). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Rocketship
titles.note: Short (11 min). Written and directed by Iris Almaraz, an East L.A. Chicana filmmaker and festival director of L.I.F.E. (Film Fatales); the project was a Sundance Writing Lab second-round finalist (Film Fatales bio, as 'Rocket Ship'). Two neglected sisters try to bring their mentally ill mother home from a playground (TMDB). about_community left for an editor (rule #6). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Hangtown
titles.note: Written and directed by Los Angeles filmmaker David Aguilar, autobiographically inspired by growing up in Placerville, California (Good Times, Watsonville Film Festival). A Latino boy who speaks no Spanish bonds with a fleeing Mexican immigrant and stands up to armed vigilantes, reliving the discrimination aimed at his immigrant parents (TMDB, Good Times). led_by left for an editor (rule #2): the press piece implies but doesn't state the director's heritage. SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.ref: STREET SMART: Lessons from a TV Icon (2025)
titles.title: STREET SMART: Lessons from a TV Icon
titles.note: Documentary written and directed by TV writer Ernie Bustamante (The 74, WLRN). Sonia Manzano's path from a South Bronx childhood to Maria on Sesame Street, the first Latina in a regular role on American TV, over 44 years, then creating Alma's Way; with Sonia Sotomayor (TMDB, The 74). Premiered at DOC NYC; Manzano received the Miami Film Festival's Impact Award. led_by not added: no source confirms the director's heritage (rule #2). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

titles.title: Lucrecia y las brujas
titles.note: Short (23 min). Written and directed by Eduardo Lecuona (TMDB credits), a Mexican filmmaker whose shorts Andrés and Bea were Morelia official selections, now a producer in Mexico City (Morelia festival profile, as Eduardo García Lecuona). A superstitious drag-bar singer seeks a cleansing from two witches before a TV audition (TMDB). No about_community (rule #6). SF Latino Film Festival 2026 lineup, requested directly.

A romance between a young mechanic and a university student from a wealthy family, divided by class (TMDB). No about_community (rule #6). Restored for Venice Classics 2026. Sundance/SXSW/Venice 2026 lineups (Remezcla, Cinema Tropical).

titles.title: Josephine
titles.note: Written and directed by Beth de Araújo, Brazilian-American (Cinema Tropical; TMDB credits). An eight-year-old who witnesses a violent assault and her parents' fight for justice (TMDB). No about_community. Sundance 2026, U.S. Dramatic Competition. Sundance/SXSW/Venice 2026 lineups (Remezcla, Cinema Tropical).

titles.title: Ritorno a Buenos Aires
titles.note: Directed by Marco Bechis, Chilean-Italian (Cinema Tropical), co-written with Vijaya Bechis Boll (TMDB); an Italy-Brazil co-production in Italian. about_community: a man returns to Argentina to testify against the soldiers who tortured him under the dictatorship (TMDB, Cinema Tropical). Venice 2026, official competition. Sundance/SXSW/Venice 2026 lineups (Remezcla, Cinema Tropical).
